# Acknowledgements {.unnumbered}

This book exists because drilling and completions reports capture far
more than operational summaries. Behind short entries such as "POOH to
change BHA due to erratic torque" sit decisions, experience, and
operational context that are obvious to the engineers involved in the
operation but often invisible to a general-purpose model that has never
seen anything like it.

Thanks are due to the open-source communities behind the tools this book
relies on throughout: Python, Quarto, Jupyter, PyTorch, Hugging Face
Transformers, PEFT, and the broader open-weight model ecosystem. None of
the engineering in this book would be reproducible without them.

Finally, thanks to every reader working through this material on their
own operational data. If you find an error, a fine-tuning claim that
doesn't hold up under evaluation, or a chapter that assumes something it
shouldn't, please open an issue in the companion repository —
corrections from practitioners are what keep a book like this honest.

The ideas, engineering examples, educational approach, and technical
validation presented in this book are the author's. AI tools, including
Claude, were used throughout the project to assist with code generation,
editing, documentation, and iterative review. All engineering decisions,
implementation choices, and final content remain the responsibility of
the author.
